tiers.title: THE SENTENCES — read these
tiers.note: On the first screens, 12 words or more. This is prose somebody wrote, and prose is where a translation can be correct word by word and still read like nobody says that.

tiers.title: The labels — skim these
tiers.note: On the same screens, shorter than a sentence. Buttons, headings, menu items. A wrong one is usually obvious; you are looking for the one that means something else in your language.

tiers.title: Further in — only if you have time
tiers.note: Reachable from these screens but deeper in: shared components, error states, things that may never appear. Listed so nothing is hidden, not because it is the best use of an hour.

screens.name: signup
screens.why: the form itself, plus the plan names beside it — the first prose anyone reads

screens.name: login
screens.why: a signup that already has an account lands here, and so does everyone on their second visit

screens.name: onboarding
screens.why: the first two minutes: the upload, the privacy sentence said before anything is handed over, and the one sentence back

screens.name: dashboard chrome
screens.why: the sidebar, top nav and banners wrap every screen after onboarding, so they are read before anything inside them

screens.name: first result
screens.why: where onboarding sends them, and the first screen that is about their data rather than about the product
